authors.name: Nicholas I. Hourwich

At the founding congress of the Communist Party of America he was elected its international delegate. With John Reed he was an American representative on the Comintern Executive Committee and participated in the Third Comintern Congress. He never returned to the United States, remained in Soviet Russia, but held no further Comintern positions..

authors.name: Rose Wortis
authors.bio: > 30 Rose Wortis was born in Ukraine and moved to New York City at the age of 8. She joined the International Ladies Garment Workers Union and was a member of the Socialist Party until the Bolshevik Revolution, when she became a communist activist. Secretary of the Trade Union Unity League from 1929, she became a well-known speaker and writer. She spent much of her life defending herself against anticommunist attack until her death in 1958.

authors.name: Angelo Braxton Herndon
authors.bio: 23 Angelo Braxton Herndon was born into a poor family in southwestern Ohio. He joined the CPUSA in 1930 and was sent to Atlanta, Georgia as a labor organizer for the Party’s Unemployment Council. Arrested, he was convicted of insurrection. The campaign for his freedom became a major cause for the Party. Herndon drifted away from the CPUSA in the early 1940s snde was expelled from the Party for "Negro nationalism."
